name: Kigali
subtitle: Kigali, capital of Rwanda: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 1,745,555 people live in the City of Kigali (counted 2022).

Kigali was reported as celebrating 100 years of existence in 2007, consistent with a 1907 founding. Another New Times history says Germany appointed Dr Richard Kandt as first imperial resident governor for Rwanda in 1906 (dates differ between sources).
Kandt was the German colonial resident in Rwanda (1906 appointment per this source).

parts.text: Kigali was reported as celebrating 100 years of existence in 2007, consistent with a 1907 founding. Another New Times history says Germany appointed Dr Richard Kandt as first imperial resident governor for Rwanda in 1906 (dates differ between sources).
Kandt was the German colonial resident in Rwanda (1906 appointment per this source).
After independence (1962) the new republic made Kigali the capital.
Rapid growth: from about 6,000 people in 1962 to roughly 1 million by 2011 (press figure); the 2022 census counted 1,745,555 residents.
Kigali has a master plan: the 2013 plan was updated (Kigali Master Plan 2050) by Surbana Jurong/SMEC; the project page lists a projected 2050 population of 3.8 million versus 1.3 million existing.

items.label: people in the City of Kigali, 2022

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in the City of Kigali?

parts.text: 1,745,555 in 2022, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Resident population of the City of Kigali (province-level unit with districts Nyarugenge, Gasabo, Kicukiro) enumerated in the Fifth Population and Housing Census as of 15 August 2022 (fieldwork 16-30 August 2022); density 2,401 per km2; 86.9% urban.

items.text: Kigali marked as founded in 1907 (centenary celebrated in 2007); Kandt, German colonial resident, associated with the founding. Sources differ on Kandt's appointment (1906 per New Times).
After independence Kigali becomes capital of the Rwandan republic; population then about 6,000.

UN Security Council Resolution 955 creates the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda to prosecute persons responsible for genocide in 1994 (genocide against the Tutsi; the page read gives the tribunal's purpose, not the phrase 'against the Tutsi').
Earlier Kigali master plan adopted (later updated as the 2050 plan).
Kigali Convention Centre opens and days later hosts the African Union Summit.
The former Presidential Palace Museum in Kanombe becomes the Rwanda Art Museum.
Fifth national census counts 1,745,555 residents in the City of Kigali (13.2% of Rwanda).
